title: First constant cohomology vanishes on closed subschemes of the spectrum of a normal domain with separably closed fraction field (Stacks 09ZB)
statement: Let $R$ be a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] whose field of fractions is separably closed [def-pc-separably-closed], let $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then for every finite abelian group $M$, with constant sheaf $\underline M$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on $Z_{\Et}$, the etale cohomology group [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] $H^1(Z_{\Et},\underline M)$ is zero.

source.place: Lemma 09ZB (label lemma-gabber-for-h1-absolutely-algebraically-closed), line 14425, and its proof (an $H^1$ class is an $\underline M$-torsor, Cohomology on Sites Lemma 03AJ; a torsor is finite locally constant, hence represented by a finite etale surjective $V\to Z$, Lemma 03RV; $V\to Z$ has a section by Lemma 09ZA, label lemma-closed-of-affine-normal-scheme-with-alg-closed-function-field, line 14390, which uses Algebra Lemma 04D1 and Lemma 09Z9)

proof.text: Let $\xi\in H^1(Z_{\Et},\underline M)$. By [thm-galois-torsor-h1] (Cohomology on Sites Lemma 03AJ), $\xi$ corresponds canonically to an isomorphism class of $\underline M$-torsors on $Z_{\Et}$. To prove that $\xi=0$, it is enough to show that the corresponding torsor is trivial.

source.place: Lemma 09ZB, proof, first sentence; Cohomology on Sites Lemma 03AJ identifies H^1 with torsors

proof.text: An $\underline M$-torsor is finite locally constant by its definition [def-weil-pbc-finite-torsors]. The equivalence between finite locally constant sheaves and finite etale schemes [thm-galois-lc-etale] therefore represents it by a finite etale surjective morphism $V\to Z$ equipped with the simply transitive $M$-action.

source.place: Lemma 09ZB, proof, first sentence; Lemma 03RV represents finite locally constant torsors by finite etale surjective schemes

proof.text: The finite etale surjection $V\to Z$ from the preceding step represents the corresponding $\underline M$-torsor as an etale sheaf. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-gabber-finite-etale-section] (Stacks 09ZA) to the closed subscheme $Z\subseteq X$; its section $s:Z\to V$ is therefore a global sheaf section of that torsor. Translation by this global section identifies the torsor with the constant torsor $\underline M$, so its class in $\operatorname{Tor}^1(Z,M)$ is the base point and $\xi=0$. Since every $\xi$ is zero, $H^1(Z_{\Et},\underline M)=0$.

source.place: Lemma 09ZB, proof, final sentence; Lemma 09ZA supplies a section, which gives a global section of the torsor and trivializes it
